header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rate and exemption: Treasury 2026 Withholding Guide: "Withholding Rate: 4.25% Personal Exemption Amount: $5,900". No standard deduction; the personal exemption is $5,900 per taxpayer, spouse and dependent for 2026 (indexed). Starts from federal AGI. Social Security benefits are not taxed. Retirement/pension subtraction: 2026 is the first year of the fully phased-in Lowering MI Costs Plan (PA 4 of 2023; Treasury: "2026 (and beyond) ... up to 100%") - regardless of birth year a taxpayer may subtract all qualifying PUBLIC pension benefits, and private retirement benefits (pensions, IRA distributions, most defined-contribution plan payments) "up to the remaining balance of $67,610 if single or married filing separately, or $135,220 if married and filing a joint return" for 2026 (Form 446); public benefits subtracted reduce that cap, which is CPI-indexed. Alternative elections not modeled: the birth-year tier rules, including the Michigan standard deduction against all income for taxpayers born after 1952 who have reached age 67, and the public-safety retiree subtraction; PA 24 of 2025 lets those 67+ claim both that standard deduction and the Social Security deduction for 2026-2028. NOT MODELED: city income taxes levied by a number of Michigan cities (e.g. Detroit) on residents and on nonresidents working there. No capital-gains exclusion. Cross-checked against Tax Foundation, "State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026" (data as of Jan 1 2026, updated Feb 11 2026).

flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: $67,610 per person ($135,220 joint) cap on private retirement income; public pensions are fully subtractable but count against the cap; minAge 59 approximates the qualified-distribution requirement (pension benefits can qualify earlier); birth-year tier and age-67 standard-deduction elections not modeled
